prompt:
Draft a procedure for continual improvement at an aerospace component manufacturer. Include data sources for improvement opportunities (audits, NCs, customer feedback, process data, benchmarking), prioritization methodology, project selection, resource allocation, implementation tracking, and effectiveness measurement. Align with ISO 9001 clause 10.3.

Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
- document (string): the complete procedure or document text
- sections (string): structured sections of the document
- clauseRefs (string): ISO clause references addressed

End your response with exactly one line: ANSWER: <your JSON object>
response:
{
  "document": "Continual Improvement Procedure

1. Purpose
This procedure establishes a systematic approach to continual improvement in alignment with ISO 9001:2015 Clause 10.3. It defines the processes for identifying, prioritizing, selecting, implementing, and measuring improvement initiatives across all manufacturing and quality systems at [Company Name].

2. Scope
Applies to all departments involved in the design, production, inspection, and delivery of aerospace components, including engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and customer service.

3. Definitions
- Continual Improvement: Ongoing effort to enhance products, services, or processes.
- Nonconformity (NC): Failure to meet a specified requirement.
- Key Performance Indicator (KPI): Quantifiable measure used to evaluate success.

4. Data Sources for Improvement Opportunities
Improvement opportunities are identified from the following data sources:
- Internal Audits: Findings from scheduled quality system audits (ISO 9001, AS9100).
- Nonconformities (NCs): Root cause analysis of NCs from production, inspection, and supplier issues.
- Customer Feedback: Complaints, surveys, warranty claims, and customer scorecards.
- Process Data: Statistical process control (SPC) charts, yield rates, cycle times, scrap/rework rates.
- Benchmarking: Comparison against industry best practices (e.g., FAA, NASA, or peer aerospace manufacturers).

5. Prioritization Methodology
Opportunities are prioritized using a Risk Priority Number (RPN) derived from:
- Severity (S): Impact on safety, compliance, or customer satisfaction (1–10)
- Occurrence (O): Frequency of occurrence (1–10)
- Detectability (D): Likelihood of current controls detecting the issue (1–10)
RPN = S × O × D
Opportunities with RPN ≥ 120 are classified as High Priority; 60–119 as Medium; <60 as Low.

6. Project Selection
- High-priority opportunities are submitted as formal Improvement Projects via the Continuous Improvement Request (CIR) form.
- A cross-functional Improvement Review Board (IRB), comprising Quality, Engineering, Production, and Operations leads, reviews CIRs monthly.
- Projects are selected based on RPN, alignment with strategic objectives, regulatory impact, and resource availability.
- Selected projects are documented in the Improvement Project Register.

7. Resource Allocation
- Each approved project is assigned a Project Owner and a cross-functional team.
- Resources (personnel, budget, equipment) are allocated based on project scope and priority.
- High-priority projects receive dedicated time (e.g., 20% FTE) and access to Lean Six Sigma tools.
- Budget requests are reviewed and approved by the Quality Manager and Operations Director.

8. Implementation Tracking
- Projects follow a structured PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) cycle.
- Milestones and deliverables are tracked using Gantt charts in the company’s project management system.
- Weekly progress reviews are held with the IRB.
- All actions, decisions, and changes are documented in the project file.

9. Effectiveness Measurement
- Each project defines 2–3 measurable KPIs prior to implementation (e.g., reduction in scrap rate, cycle time, customer complaints).
- KPIs are monitored for 3 months post-implementation.
- Effectiveness is evaluated using pre- and post-implementation data.
- Projects are deemed successful if KPIs improve by ≥15% and sustain for 3 consecutive months.
- Results are reported in the Monthly Quality Review and documented in the Improvement Archive.

10. Documentation and Records
- CIR forms, project registers, KPI reports, and review minutes are retained for a minimum of 10 years.
- All records are accessible via the Quality Management System (QMS) portal.

11. Review and Update
This procedure is reviewed annually by the Quality Manager or more frequently if regulatory or operational changes occur.

12. References
- ISO 9001:2015 Clause 10.3
- AS9100D
- Company QMS Manual, Section 8.5.1

Approved by: [Quality Director]
Effective Date: [Date]
Revision: 1.0",
